population: Unselected (higher-risk MDS on azacitidine combinations; lower-risk and refractory MDS on monotherapy)
note: Three pan-HDAC inhibitors reached MDS: pracinostat (randomized phase 2 with azacitidine negative, CR 18% vs 33%; a 45 mg single-arm follow-on stopped by the sponsor), panobinostat (no responses as monotherapy in lower-risk or refractory MDS, no survival benefit with azacitidine; approved in myeloma, whose dog QT/GI toxicology supplies the safety comparison) and ivaltinostat (CG-745 plus azacitidine phase 1/2 NCT02737462, no results found).
label: MDS (pan-HDAC)

engagement.note: Pracinostat accumulated in mouse tumour tissue and gave sustained histone (de)acetylation change; no patient comparison yet.
engagement.quote: In contrast to SAHA, SB939 accumulates in tumor tissue and induces a sustained inhibition of histone acetylation in tumor tissue.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (Mol Cancer Ther paywalled); the abstract's 'inhibition of histone acetylation' is quoted as printed.
engagement.judgement: The pracinostat program's model system is the S*BIO mouse xenograft platform; it opens on the 2010 colorectal paper because that is where the PK/PD readout (tumour histone acetylation) was set.

engagement.note: In 44 AML/MDS patients plasma pracinostat rose with dose but histone acetylation did not follow; solid-tumour phase 1 saw no AcH3-dose relation either.
engagement.quote: Despite a dose-dependent increase in the plasma concentration of pracinostat, a similar increase in histone acetylation was not observed.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (Cancer; PMC author manuscript not read). Razak 2011 (solid tumours, PBMC AcH3) reported no clear relationship between AcH3 changes and dose level.
engagement.judgement: Scored contra because the mouse readout (sustained, exposure-driven histone acetylation) did not reproduce in dosed patients: acetylation changed in some, but not with dose (Abaza 2017 in 25 AML + 24 MDS; Razak 2011 in solid tumours). A lenient reader scores same with source_calls_it partial, since the readout did move in some patients. Pairing is mine; the trial papers do not cite the mouse PD data.
engagement.magnitude_basis: Histone acetylation in blood cells vs plasma exposure

engagement.model: Human leukemia cells ex vivo (K562, primary AML blasts)
engagement.note: Panobinostat depleted DNMT1/EZH2 and de-repressed JunB in leukemia cells, alone and with decitabine; no MDS patient comparison yet.
engagement.short: Panobinostat PD set in leukemia cells
engagement.quote: Here, we determined that the pan-HDAC inhibitor panobinostat (LBH589) treatment depletes DNMT1 and EZH2 protein levels, disrupts the interaction of DNMT1 with EZH2, as well as de-represses JunB in human acute leukemia cells.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (Cancer Biol Ther; PMC author manuscript not read). Panobinostat leukemia-cell work predates this paper (the 2006 phase 1 already cites cell-line activity); 2009 is the earliest verified HMA-combination model paper.
engagement.judgement: A separate track from the pracinostat xenografts: a different system (ex vivo human leukemia cells, Bhalla laboratory) making a different prediction (HDAC inhibition plus a hypomethylating agent).

engagement.model: Human leukemia cells ex vivo (K562, primary AML blasts)
engagement.note: In 39 AML/high-risk MDS patients on panobinostat plus azacitidine, histone H3/H4 acetylation rose and tracked clinical response.
engagement.quote: Increased histone H3 and H4 acetylation was a useful early biomarker of clinical response.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of an open-access paper. Giles 2006 (IV panobinostat, 13 AML/1 MDS) had already shown H3/H2B acetylation rising in CD34+ blasts; Dimicoli 2012 (13 lower-risk MDS, oral) found acetylation 'not consistently' induced.
engagement.judgement: Called same on the weight of two patient series (Giles 2006, Tan 2014) showing the cell-model readout (histone acetylation) moving in dosed patients; Dimicoli 2012's inconsistent Western blots in lower-risk MDS are noted but do not reverse the direction. Pairing is mine.
engagement.magnitude_basis: Histone H3/H4 acetylation in patient blood cells

engagement.note: SB939 acH3 tracked dose in HCT-116 and HL-60 mouse tissues; in 30 solid-tumour phase 1 patients PBMC acH3 rose with dose (10-80 mg).
engagement.quote: When applied to PBMCs from 30 patients with advanced solid malignancies in a phase I clinical trial, a dose-dependent (10-80 mg) increase in relative acH3 was observed 3-hour postdose on day 1
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (Mol Cancer Ther, PMID 21586629, epub 2011-05-17, print 2011-07-01). Subjects are solid-tumour patients, not MDS; engagement admits any dosed humans. The same paper reports the mouse tissue data, so the comparison is stated.
engagement.judgement: Stated comparison: the authors measured the same acH3 Western readout in the xenograft/orthotopic HL-60 mice and in phase 1 PBMCs and conclude the PD 'translated from preclinical models to patients'; the readout moved with dose (r=0.97 with Cmax/AUC), so same. The later Abaza 2017 entry (adjudicated same) follows it on this track.
engagement.magnitude_basis: Relative acH3 in PBMCs vs SB939 dose and plasma Cmax/AUC

dose.note: Mouse PK set the exposure case for pracinostat: >4-fold bioavailability and 3.3-fold half-life over vorinostat, efficacy at the mouse MTD.
dose.short: Mouse PK sets the exposure case
dose.quote: It has very favorable pharmacokinetic properties after oral dosing in mice, with >4-fold increased bioavailability and 3.3-fold increased half-life over suberoylanilide hydroxamic acid (SAHA).
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; the abstract reports 94% tumour growth inhibition at the mouse maximum tolerated dose, i.e. efficacy was shown at, not below, the MTD.

dose.model: Multi-species allometric scaling plus Simcyp PBPK prediction of pracinostat human oral PK, from mouse/rat/dog in-vivo PK and human in-vitro ADME (S*BIO, Jayaraman 2011)
dose.note: Human oral PK predicted from mouse/rat/dog ADME by allometry and Simcyp agreed with the phase 1 data; 60 mg RP2D reached.
dose.quote: The predicted oral PK profile and parameters of SB939, using Simcyp and allometric scaling, were in good agreement with observed data in humans.
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (Drug Metab Dispos paywalled); no fold-difference is given, so magnitude is left null. Patient PK is the solid-tumour phase 1 (Razak 2011, RPTD 60 mg).
dose.judgement: The source itself compares predicted and observed human PK, so comparison_stated is true. Scored as the exposure target being reached in humans; the 2017 entry then records that reaching it did not translate.
dose.magnitude_basis: Predicted vs observed human oral PK (AUC, half-life); no fold reported in the abstract

dose.model: Human leukemia cells ex vivo (K562, primary AML blasts)
dose.note: Cell-culture concentrations only; the model stated no exposure or occupancy target for patients.
dose.quote: Combined treatment with panobinostat and decitabine caused greater attenuation of DNMT1 and EZH2 levels than either agent alone, which was accompanied by more JunB de-repression and loss of clonogenic survival of K562 cells.
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; the concentrations used are not in the abstract.

dose.model: Multi-species allometric scaling plus Simcyp PBPK prediction of pracinostat human oral PK, from mouse/rat/dog in-vivo PK and human in-vitro ADME (S*BIO, Jayaraman 2011)
dose.population: Unselected (model: mouse, rat, dog PK; human microsomes, hepatocytes, Caco-2)
dose.quote: The oral bioavailability was 34, 65, and ∼3% in mice, dogs, and rats, respectively.
dose.note: Mouse, rat and dog PK plus human in-vitro ADME fed Simcyp and allometry to predict pracinostat's human oral PK; no efficacy exposure or tolerability margin stated.
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (Drug Metab Dispos, paywalled, not in PMC). 2011 is a publication proxy: the ADME work is IND-enabling by nature and the first-in-human studies started in 2007 (NCT00741234 2007-04, NCT00504296 2007-09), but the date the Simcyp/allometric prediction was run is not public. Pracinostat never reached an NDA, so model_filed is unknown.
dose.judgement: Split from pracinostat-mouse-xenograft under this run's identity rule: a genuinely different system (three-species in-vivo PK and human in-vitro ADME run through Simcyp and allometry, no tumour) making a different prediction (human CL, Vss, bioavailability and the oral PK profile, not tumour growth or tumour acetylation). Same precedent as famitinib-pbpk-rat-monkey-human-pk and gdc0980-genentech-translational-pkpd in this run. The draft's dose entry 2 (Jayaraman 2011, same) sits on the xenograft model_id and is the entry this track re-keys; removing it there is the adjudicator's edit.

efficacy.note: Pracinostat alone shrank FLT3-ITD and JAK2-mutant AML xenografts and synergized with pacritinib; the MDS trials rested on this and on class-level HMA synergy.
efficacy.quote: High efficacy of the HDACi pracinostat treating AML and synergy with the JAK2/FLT3 inhibitor pacritinib is demonstrated.
efficacy.confidence_note: Open-access abstract read. No MDS-specific model (SKM-1, MDS-L, primary MDS CD34+) for pracinostat was found; the phase 2 paper cites class-level in vitro HDACi-azacitidine synergy and 'preclinical activity in myeloid malignancies'.
efficacy.judgement: Opens the efficacy strip at 2012 rather than 2010 because the 2010 paper's efficacy models were colorectal; the track slug and first-use year stay those of the xenograft platform.

efficacy.note: Randomized, placebo-controlled phase 2 in 102 higher-risk MDS patients: CR by cycle 6 was 18% with pracinostat vs 33% with placebo, no OS or PFS gain.
efficacy.quote: The CR rate by cycle 6 of therapy was 18% and 33% (P = .07) in the pracinostat and placebo groups, respectively.
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC5432122). NCT01873703 has no registry results; NCT03151304 (45 mg, single-arm) posted results 2022-03-02.
efficacy.reason: CR lower than placebo in MDS
efficacy.judgement: Pairing is mine: the trial paper cites pracinostat's 'preclinical activity in myeloid malignancies' and class-level HDACi-HMA synergy but makes no model comparison. The direction reversed (CR 18% vs 33%), so magnitude is 'opposite'. The HMA-failure phase 2 (Yalniz 2020, CR 2%) and the 45 mg single-arm follow-on (ORR 35.9%, no comparator, ended by sponsor) are listed as patient_trials and change nothing; the AML phase 3 PRIMULA futility stop is outside this disease.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: CR rate by cycle 6: 18% pracinostat vs 33% placebo

patient_trials.quote: The combination of azacitidine with pracinostat did not improve outcomes in patients with higher-risk MDS.
Adding pracinostat to HMAs did not improve outcomes in patients previously treated with HMAs.
Sponsor's decision as at the completion of the primary analysis, the data were considered mature

efficacy.model: Human leukemia cells ex vivo (K562, primary AML blasts)
efficacy.note: Panobinostat with decitabine killed K562 and primary AML cells but spared normal CD34+ progenitors; no MDS patient comparison yet.
efficacy.short: Combination kills AML cells, spares CD34+
efficacy.quote: Collectively, these findings indicate that co-treatment with panobinostat and decitabine targets multiple epigenetic mechanisms to de-repress JunB and exerts antileukemia activity against human acute myeloid leukemia cells.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. No MDS-specific panobinostat model (SKM-1, MDS-L, primary MDS CD34+ cells, MDS xenograft) was found in Europe PMC; the MDS trials ran on AML-cell and class-level data.

efficacy.model: Human leukemia cells ex vivo (K562, primary AML blasts)
efficacy.note: Single-agent panobinostat: 1 of 13 lower-risk MDS patients improved; 0 of 26 refractory MDS responded; with azacitidine, no OS or progression benefit and more deaths.
efficacy.short: No responses in MDS; combination no OS gain
efficacy.quote: This data indicates that panobinostat at the dose and schedule studied here has limited activity in lower risk MDS.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of Dimicoli 2012 and Garcia-Manero 2017 (Leukemia, open access); registry results for NCT00594230, NCT01034657 and NCT00946647 read directly. Platzbecker 2014 (Leukemia letter) has no abstract and was not read.
efficacy.reason: No responses; combination no OS gain
efficacy.judgement: Track scored contra on the earliest MDS comparison (Dimicoli, epub 2011) and held there: 0/26 refractory MDS (NCT00594230, interim futility stop), 0% HI-E in transfusion-dependent lower-risk MDS (NCT01034657, stopped for lack of efficacy), and the randomized phase 2b with azacitidine (NCT00946647) showing no 1-year OS or TTP difference with more on-treatment deaths. The phase 2b composite CR was numerically higher (27.5% vs 14.3%, overlapping CIs), which a lenient reader scores same/partial; rejected because the sponsor abandoned the regimen and the model's single-agent prediction had already failed. Tan 2014 (ORR 5/10 MDS, single-arm) is uncontrolled. Pairing is mine.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: ORR 1/13 (HI only), 0/26 and 0% HI-E as monotherapy; 1-year OS 60% vs 70% with azacitidine

patient_trials.quote: Of the 13 patients, 1 (8%) achieved hematological improvement (HI-E and HI-P, duration 3 months) and 6 (46%) had stable disease for a median duration of 6 months (range 1.7–13.6).
Per protocol, the results of a planned interim analysis demonstrated insufficient efficacy and led to early termination of the study.
The study was terminated due to lack of efficacy of single agent LBH589
However, no significant difference was observed in the 1-year OS rate (PAN+AZA, 60% (50-80%); AZA, 70% (50-80%)) or time to progression (PAN+AZA, 70% (40-90%); AZA, 70% (40-80%)).

safety.model: Dog telemetry and rat/dog repeat-dose toxicology (panobinostat IND package)
safety.note: IV panobinostat phase 1 (13 AML, 1 MDS) hit grade 3 QTcF prolongation as its DLT; the animal cardiovascular data were not yet public.
safety.short: Patient QTc DLT, animal data unpublished
safety.quote: Four dose-limiting toxicities (grade 3 QTcF prolongation) were observed, four at 14.0 mg/m(2) and one at 11.5 mg/m(2).
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. Proxy opener: the toxicology package had to exist for this IND, but its content was first made public in the 2015 FDA review, so no comparison was possible before then.
safety.judgement: Opened at 2006 as a proxy for first use of the toxicology package; the comparison itself is the 2015 entry.

safety.model: Dog telemetry and rat/dog repeat-dose toxicology (panobinostat IND package)
safety.note: FDA's review pairs dog QTc prolongation (up to 25 msec) and GI target-organ toxicity with patient QTc and diarrhea, the boxed harms; thyroid, marrow and skin findings did not appear.
safety.short: Dog QTc and GI matched patient harms
safety.quote: In telemetered dogs, QTc prolongation of up to 25 msec was observed in panobinostat treated animals. QTc prolongation has been reported in patients treated with panobinostat.
safety.confidence_note: Pharmacology review downloaded and grepped (not in the source bundle; the label 205353s000lbl.txt is). Label section 13.2 lists thyroid, bone marrow and skin findings 'observed in animals and not reported (or reported with low incidence) in patients'.
safety.reason: Dog QTc and GI matched patient harms
safety.judgement: Imported from multiple myeloma (Farydak NDA 205353): the regulator states the dog-patient QTc comparison itself, and names the GI tract among animal target organs while severe diarrhea carries the boxed warning. Scored same with source_calls_it partial because the same package over-predicted thyroid, marrow and skin harms that patients did not show; a stricter reader scores that contra (magnitude opposite). In MDS itself, QTc prolongation withheld panobinostat in 1 of 13 lower-risk patients (Dimicoli 2012) and the azacitidine combination carried more grade 3/4 events and on-treatment deaths (Garcia-Manero 2017). Pracinostat's excess grade >=3 events (98% vs 74%) and discontinuations in MDS were never compared with its mouse tolerability data, which are abstract-level only, so that track stays untested.
safety.magnitude_basis: QTc: up to 25 msec in dogs vs QTcF increase of 31-60 msec in 14.5% of myeloma patients (label 6.1)

safety.note: Mouse tolerability (efficacy at the MTD) was never compared with pracinostat's excess grade >=3 events and discontinuations in MDS.
safety.quote: SB939 is a new hydroxamic acid based histone deacetylase inhibitor with improved physicochemical, pharmaceutical, and pharmacokinetic properties.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; whether the mouse studies reported GI or constitutional toxicity at effective doses could not be checked, so the model's silence on the MDS harms is unverified.
safety.judgement: Kept untested rather than contra: the harm that sank pracinostat in MDS (grade >=3 events 98% vs 74%, discontinuation 20% vs 10%; fatigue, nausea and diarrhoea at the RPTD in Razak 2011) is counted nowhere else, but the mouse data were not readable enough to say the model was silent on it.
